source.idea: A premium, original, cinematic side-scrolling arcade platformer for the web — an 8-episode campaign with story, power-ups, a boss and credits — governed by the Ruslan Magana Definitions.

references.note: SNES/Sega-style parallax city, lit windows, sun glow, pixel tiles

goal_analysis.real_goal: Prove that a governed AI pipeline can ship a coherent, premium platformer — not a primitive prototype — by designing the whole solution before any batch runs.
goal_analysis.audience: Enterprises evaluating safe, scalable AI-built software.
missing_decisions: art direction (the v1 prototype had none → flat look, overlapping title, slivered coins)
level architecture (how do levels scale without rewriting the engine?)
visual acceptance target (what does 'done' LOOK like?)
batch ownership map (which batch owns which file?)

risks.risk: Each batch improvises because there is no authoritative design.
risks.mitigation: Freeze art direction + entity contracts + asset manifest in this bundle before batching.

risks.risk: Adding levels means sprawling, ungoverned edits.
risks.mitigation: Levels are DATA (episode config objects) read by a fixed engine; adding one = adding one object.

risks.risk: Single-file game cannot scale past a prototype.
risks.mitigation: Use a real engine (Phaser + Vite + TS) with scenes/entities/levels.

framework_decision.rationale: 2D arcade with tilemaps, sprites, camera, particles, mobile controls, and GitHub Pages-compatible static output. Phaser gives the scene/entity/physics systems for free; Vite+TS give a typed, CI-friendly build.

rejected.why_not: Great for a prototype/jam, but cannot carry an 8-episode campaign without becoming an ungoverned mega-file (this was the v1 failure).
Heavyweight for a 2D web arcade; large bundles; slower governed iteration.

visual_target.style: SNES/Sega-inspired cinematic pixel-art platformer; warm sunset palette; layered parallax.
must_include: robot hero (rounded body, glowing blue visor, yellow helmet)
layered parallax city with MANY warm lit windows + sun glow + light rays
round gold Contract Coins in arcs (never edge-on / never slivers)
holographic contract panels (rules, contract.yaml, access log)
animated Matrix Gate portal at level end
footer: coded by GitPilot — under a Matrix Builder contract

architecture.diagram: idea -> Title -> Story(ep) -> Game(ep) -> (gate) -> Story(ep+1) ... -> Victory -> Credits

entities.name: EpisodeCfg
entities.purpose: The DATA contract for one episode — engine reads it, never changes.

functional: 8 episodes load in order, simplest to hardest
hero runs / variable-jumps / double-jumps; coins collect; enemies stomp; shield protects
episode VIII boss (Rogue Architect) → Victory → scrolling Credits
npm run typecheck clean; npm run build produces dist/; zero runtime errors
visual: coins render ROUND in arcs (never slivers)
title does not overlap itself; parallax city with lit windows + sun glow visible
footer reads exactly: coded by GitPilot — under a Matrix Builder contract
performance: steady 60fps on desktop; DPR-aware crisp scaling on mobile
accessibility: on-screen touch controls on small screens
